---
title: "What if we fix the tail, price the throw, and optimise the wing instead?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# Tail held at conservative proportions, release speed priced against elevation,
# and the wing given taper and a station to move to. Each arm is re-flown through
# the marched model, which is what says whether any of it is real.
plain = wing_study(free_wing=False)
shaped = wing_study(free_wing=True)

assert abs(shaped["gap"]) < 0.02        # collocated and marched now agree
assert abs(plain["gap"]) < 0.02         # and not only for the shaped wing
assert shaped["marched"] > plain["marched"]          # shaping the wing pays
assert shaped["launch_angle"] < 1.0     # priced, the best throw is flat
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{shaped['marched']:.2f}"` s]{.hero-value}
[time aloft, and the marched model agrees to `{python} f"{abs(shaped['gap']):.1%}"`]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** The disagreement disappears. Priced against elevation the best throw
is flat, a flat launch never excites the pitch mode, and the two models close to
[`{python} f"{abs(shaped['gap']):.1%}"`]{.key} where they stood 194% apart
(@tbl-wing). Shaping the wing buys
`{python} f"{shaped['marched'] - plain['marched']:.2f}"` s and wants more: taper
sits on its bound at `{python} f"{shaped['taper']:.2f}"`. Ballast goes the other
way from expected, to `{python} f"{shaped['ballast'] * 1e3:.1f}"` g.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The throw model is doing the work
Invented for this entry, it flipped the optimum and closed the gap. It wants measuring.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Speed falls `{python} f"{THROW_DROP:.0%}"`** by the steepest throw.
2. **Tail held** at McEagle proportions.
3. **Bounds on aspect, taper, ballast** are mine.
4. **One start** per solve; basins exist.
:::

```{python}

md_table(["", "aspect only", "+ taper, station"], [

    ("taper", f"{plain['taper']:.2f}", f"{shaped['taper']:.2f}"),
    ("ballast, g", f"{plain['ballast'] * 1e3:.2f}", f"{shaped['ballast'] * 1e3:.2f}"),
])
```
